items.title: CdSe/ZnS starting dispersion
items.text: The starting CdSe/ZnS nanocrystals were synthesized in TOPO following references 1 and 11–13. This article does not reproduce their core-growth or ZnS-shell recipes. Stock is stored at room temperature in butanol/TOPO, approximately 1:2 v/v, at 5–10 mg CdSe cores per mL of solution. The mass basis is CdSe cores, not the total coated-particle mass. The stock remains stable for months without oxidation precautions; aged stocks were used in this work.

items.title: Core/shell/coating identity and structural limits
items.text: The reported architecture is CdSe core/ZnS shell with a silica-containing outer layer, or an alternative MPA ligand layer. The main article supplies TEM-derived core/core-shell diameters and AFM height distributions, but no source-specific atomic coordinates, unit-cell refinement, XRD or SAED pattern. A crystalline phase or downloadable measured CIF cannot be inferred from the architecture name alone. The abstract describes CdSe cores of 2–5 nm and study-wide overall coated sizes of 6–17 nm. The introduction describes silica shells of about 2–5 nm, while the abstract and discussion summarize about 1–5 nm; these are differently scoped summaries.

items.title: Conclusions within their experimental scope
items.text: The paper concludes that silica-coated particles retain blue-to-dark-red emission, about 32 nm widths and useful stability over months of storage and hours of illumination. Its phrase quantum yields of a few tens of percent does not replace the exact Table 1 values of 5–18%. The abstract’s physiological-salt claim above 150 mM and introductory stability through 200 mM summarize selected cohorts. MPA exchange is easier, while silica shows better buffer robustness in the comparisons. Recent DNA coupling and programmable assemblies remain future context without a new quantified protocol here.
